title: Radio Frequency and Modulation Systems—Part 1: Earth Stations and Spacecraft
organisation: Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS)
status_notes: The Document Control table (PDF pp. 7-11) traces the book from its original issue (January 1987) through issue 32. Issue 31 is labelled 'Current issue' (updates 2.5.6B and 3.1.6B), and issue 32 (October 2021) 'Current draft update': it updates recommendations 2.4.18 and 2.4.23 and adds the new recommendations 2.6.13 and 2.6.15. Substantive changes are marked with change bars, except in 2.6.13 and 2.6.15, which are wholly new. Each recommendation also carries its own issue and date in its page footer (for example 401 (2.1.1) B-1, January 1987; 401 (2.4.18) B-6, October 2021).

key_points.text: Issue 32 updates recommendations 2.4.18 and 2.4.23 and adds 2.6.13 and 2.6.15.
Part 1 targets conventional near-Earth and deep-space missions with moderate communications requirements; Part 2 is to cover data relay satellites.
Newer recommendations follow the nomenclature of the CCSDS Publications Manual (A20.0-Y-4); older ones keep the conventions of the original Blue Book.
Recommendations are grouped as technical (section 2), policy (section 3) and procedural (section 4); a page label such as 2.5.3A-1 encodes section, subsection, position, mission category and page.

Category A missions are at an altitude below 2.0 x 10^6 km and Category B missions at or beyond it, matching the Deep Space boundary set by WARC ORB-88 and effective on 16 March 1990; a recommendation without an A or B suffix applies to both.
Agencies shall support phase modulation with a residual carrier on Earth-to-space links.
Telecommand subcarriers are PSK-modulated sine waves of 8 kHz or 16 kHz.
Telecommand data use NRZ-L or NRZ-M on PSK subcarriers, with attention to the symbol transition density.
Low-rate telecommand coded symbol rates are 4000/2^n symbol/s (n = 0 to 9), with symbol and subcarrier transitions coinciding; 4000 symbol/s only with the 16 kHz subcarrier.
Medium-rate telecommand uses PCM/PM/bi-phase-L directly on the carrier at 4000 x 2^n coded symbol/s (n = 1 to 6).
When a residual-carrier system is insufficient, telecommand uses BPSK up to 2.048 coded Msymbol/s at 1000 x 2^n coded symbol/s (n = 0 to 11).

Space-to-Earth links: at most 64 consecutive identical coded symbols; at least 125 (Category A) or 275 (Category B) transitions per 1000 coded symbols; pseudo-randomizer use as in the TM Synchronization and Channel Coding standard.

Above 2 coded Msymbol/s, Category A space research downlinks use GMSK (BTs = 0.25, precoded), baseband-filtered OQPSK or SRRC-8PSK to meet the SFCG spectrum mask; SFCG limits the 8450-8500 MHz band to 10 MHz per mission.
EES 8 GHz high-rate downlinks use SRRC-filtered 4D-8PSK TCM, QPSK, OQPSK, 8PSK, 16/32/64APSK or filtered OQPSK to meet the SFCG mask and protect the adjacent deep-space band above 8400 MHz.

Telemetry ranging records the uplink PN range-code phase and the frame counter of a TM or AOS frame on board; it can reach 1 m standard deviation at 200 ksymbol/s or more and costs up to 4 percent of telemetry throughput.
The transponder turnaround frequency ratio for the 2025-2120/2200-2300 MHz bands is 221/240, needed only for missions requiring cross support and coherent two-way links.
New in issue 32: flexible turnaround ratios with '749' in the numerator for multiple spacecraft per aperture in the 7/8 GHz bands (2.6.13).
New in issue 32: 2407/2800 and 2407/2816 ratios for coherent 23.15-23.55 GHz forward and 27.0-27.5 GHz return inter-satellite links, for example lunar orbit-surface proximity links (2.6.15).
Category B missions in the 2, 7, 8, 32 and 34 GHz bands select frequencies from the channel frequency plan of table 3.1.6B-1, coordinated through an organisation such as the SFCG.
All relevant spacecraft-Earth station compatibility tests of table 3.5.1-1 shall be performed before cross support.
The uniform link Design Control Table is used to exchange link budgets between agencies, with 3-sigma tolerances for telecommand and 2-sigma for all other systems.
Uncertain link parameters are modelled with uniform, triangular or truncated Gaussian probability density functions, with default assignments per budget line.

notes: The normative RF reference of the library items ccsds-131-0-131x0b5 and ccsds-131-0-131x0b6ec1 (reference [5]); ccsds-231-0-231x0b4e1 and ccsds-231-0-231x0b4e1c1 cite the older issue 30. The book is assembled from recommendations of very different vintages, each with its own footer issue and date (from 1987 to 2021), and some footers are inconsistent (the contents page footer reads 'CCSDS 401 B Page xii February 2020'). In the Document Control table, issue 31 is labelled 'Current issue' and issue 32 'Current draft update', although this is the published issue 32; the year column for issues 30 to 32 is partly lost in extraction. Placeholder pages exist for reserved numbers (for example 'RESERVED for RECOMMENDATION 401 (2.2.1)'), and several recommendations are marked DELETED (for example 2.1.8A, 2.1.8B, 2.4.4, 2.4.5, 3.1.3A, 3.1.5B, 3.3.3A, 3.3.4, 2.6.12). The table of contents prints '2.1.4.B' for 2.1.4B. Only five formal reference entries exist (three in the front matter and two in 4.1.4); other documents (CCSDS coding books, 413.x and 414.1 ranging documents, SFCG recommendations, ITU-R SA.509) are cited inline and recorded as 'mentioned'. The Mission Categories figure (1.5-1) and most plots are not extracted. PDF pages 1 and 2 are duplicate covers; the extraction has 323 PDF pages (registry: 322). No individual authors are named.
